gloss: save, deliver, help; salvation, deliverance, victory
summary: To save: to bring someone out of the hand of an enemy or out of distress, so that they are free and safe. It is first rescue in war, as when Yahweh saved Israel from Egypt at the sea (Exo 14:30) or when Israel, blowing the trumpets in battle, would be remembered before Yahweh “and saved from your enemies” (Num 10:9); then any help given to one who cries out, and at last saving from sin and uncleanness and from death (Ezk 37:23; Isa 25:8–9). Scripture says again and again that salvation belongs to Yahweh and not to horse, sword or man, and that the saviors he raises up are his gift (Pro 21:31; Isa 43:11; Jdg 3:9). The nouns יְשׁוּעָה, יֵשַׁע and תְּשׁוּעָה are that salvation, deliverance or victory; Arabic wasiʿa “be wide, ample” and Sabaean and Moabite use of the root suggest its picture is bringing out of a strait place into room.

words.summary: Used only in the hiphil, “save”, and its passive the niphal, “be saved”; there is no qal. The hiphil participle מוֹשִׁיעַ is “savior”, a title Yahweh claims for himself and gives to the men he raises up.

senses.gloss: save, deliver from an enemy; give victory
senses.definition: To bring a people or a man out of the hand of an enemy or oppressor, by defeating him: the commonest use, most often with Yahweh as the one who saves.

evidence.note: “Yahweh וַיּוֹשַׁע Israel that day מִיַּד מִצְרָיִם, out of the hand of Egypt, and Israel saw Egypt dead on the seashore.”
“Yahweh raised up judges, and they saved them מִיַּד שֹׁסֵיהֶם, out of the hand of those who plundered them.”
Yahweh was with the judge and saved them from their enemies all his days, for he had pity on their groaning.
“So Yahweh saved Israel that day, and the battle passed over to Beth-aven.”
After David's victories over Aram: “Yahweh saved David wherever he went”: gave him victory.
David to Goliath: “Yahweh does not save with sword and spear, for the battle is Yahweh's.”
“I will save them by Yahweh their God, and will not save them by bow, sword, war, horses or horsemen.”
Israel did not take the land by its sword, “nor did their arm save them, but your right hand and your arm.”
“He saved them from the hand of the hater, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy”: parallel גָּאַל.
Gibeon to Joshua: “come up to us quickly, וְהוֹשִׁיעָה לָּנוּ וְעָזְרֵנוּ, save us and help us, for the kings of the Amorites have gathered against us.”
“Yahweh is our judge, Yahweh our lawgiver, Yahweh our king; he will save us.”

senses.definition: To come to the aid of someone in trouble who calls for help, between men as well as from God: rescue from a wrong being done, from need, or from affliction.

evidence.note: The shepherds drove Jethro's daughters away, “but Moses stood up וַיּוֹשִׁעָן, and helped them, and watered their flock.”
The betrothed girl in the field “cried out, and there was none to save her”, וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ לָהּ.
In the famine a woman cries to the king on the wall, “הוֹשִׁיעָה, my lord the king!”; he answers “If Yahweh does not save you, from where shall I save you?” (v. 27).
The woman of Tekoa falls before David: “הוֹשִׁעָה, O king!”: a plea for the king's judgment in her favour.
“This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard, and saved him out of all his troubles.”
The king “shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor”: saving is the king's just judgment for the weak.
“Yahweh keeps the simple; I was brought low, and he saved me.”
“Man and beast you save, Yahweh”: keep alive, preserve.
God saves the needy from the sword of their mouth and from the hand of the mighty.

senses.definition: The participle as a noun: one who saves. Yahweh raises up such a man when Israel cries out to him, or sends him; and Yahweh himself is the savior beside whom there is no other.

evidence.note: “Israel cried to Yahweh, and Yahweh raised up a מוֹשִׁיעַ for Israel, and he saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz.”
Yahweh raised up a מוֹשִׁיעַ for them, Ehud son of Gera.
“Yahweh gave Israel a מוֹשִׁיעַ, and they came out from under the hand of Aram.”
“In your great mercies you gave them מוֹשִׁיעִים, and they saved them from the hand of their adversaries.”
When Egypt cries to Yahweh because of oppressors, “he will send them a מוֹשִׁיעַ and a great one, and he will deliver (וְהִצִּילָם) them.”
“מוֹשִׁעִים shall come up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingdom shall be Yahweh's.”
“I, I am Yahweh, and beside me there is no מוֹשִׁיעַ.”
“A righteous God and a מוֹשִׁיעַ, there is none beside me.”
“I am Yahweh your God from the land of Egypt; you shall know no god but me, and there is no מוֹשִׁיעַ beside me.”
“You shall know that I, Yahweh, am your מוֹשִׁיעַ and your Redeemer (גֹאֲלֵךְ), the Mighty One of Jacob.”
“Hope of Israel, its מוֹשִׁיעַ in time of distress.”
“They forgot God their מוֹשִׁיעַ, who had done great things in Egypt.”
The enemies “cried out, but there was none to save (וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ), to Yahweh, but he did not answer them.”

senses.gloss: save oneself by one's own hand
senses.definition: With “my hand” or “your right hand” as subject and a dative of the person: to get oneself out of a wrong or a danger by one's own strength, taking into one's own hands what belongs to God. Scripture uses it as what a man should not do.

evidence.note: Abigail to David: Yahweh “has kept you from coming into blood, וְהוֹשֵׁעַ יָדְךָ לָךְ, and your hand saving for you”: avenging himself on Nabal.
David: “blessed are you, who kept me this day from coming into blood וְהֹשֵׁעַ יָדִי לִי.”
Gideon's army is cut down “lest Israel boast against me, saying, יָדִי הוֹשִׁיעָה לִּי, my own hand has saved me.”
Yahweh to Job: if you can do what I do, “then I too will praise you, that your own right hand can save you.”
The opposite course: “Do not say, I will repay evil; wait for Yahweh, and he will save you.”

senses.definition: To save a people out of the uncleanness and the sins they live in, cleansing them, so that they are Yahweh's people.

evidence.note: “They shall no more defile themselves with their idols … וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּי אֹתָם out of all their dwellings in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them, and they shall be my people.”
“I will save you from all your uncleannesses.”
The angel gives the reason for the name Ἰησοῦς (Hebrew יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, “Yahweh saves”): “for he shall save (σώσει) his people from their sins”.

senses.definition: The imperative הוֹשִׁיעָה, alone or with נָא, as the cry of one in need to God or the king.

evidence.note: “אָנָּא יַהְוֶה הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא, O Yahweh, save now! O Yahweh, send prosperity now!” The crowds cry it to Jesus as ὡσαννά (Mat 21:9).
“הוֹשִׁיעָה יַהְוֶה, for the godly man has ceased.”
“Proclaim, praise, and say: הוֹשַׁע יַהְוֶה, save your people, the remnant of Israel.”
“Yahweh, save; let the king answer us in the day we call.”
“Save us, Yahweh our God, and gather us from the nations.”

senses.gloss: be saved, delivered (from enemies, from distress)
senses.definition: To be brought out of the hand of an enemy or out of a time of distress; the passive of the hiphil's commonest sense.

evidence.note: “When you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you shall be remembered before Yahweh your God, וְנוֹשַׁעְתֶּם מֵאֹיְבֵיכֶם, and you shall be saved from your enemies.”
“Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people נוֹשַׁע בַּיַהְוֶה, saved by Yahweh, the shield of your help?”
“I call on Yahweh, who is worthy to be praised, and I am saved from my enemies.” Also 2Sa 22:4.
“The king is not saved (נוֹשָׁע) by the size of an army; a mighty man is not delivered (יִנָּצֵל) by great strength”: parallel נִצַּל.
“It is a time of distress for Jacob, but out of it he shall be saved.”
“The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.”
Zion's king comes “righteous וְנוֹשָׁע, and saved [or victorious], lowly and riding on a donkey”.
In the days of the righteous Branch “Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely”. Also Jer 33:16.

senses.definition: To be saved as the outcome of turning to Yahweh, trusting him, and having the heart made clean: salvation that follows repentance, and in Isaiah reaches the ends of the earth.

evidence.note: “Turn to me וְהִוָּשְׁעוּ, and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other.”
“In returning (שׁוּבָה) and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength; but you would not.”
“Wash your heart from wickedness, Jerusalem, that you may be saved.”
“Israel is saved by Yahweh with an everlasting salvation (תְּשׁוּעַת עוֹלָמִים); you shall not be ashamed.”
“God, restore us, and make your face shine, and we shall be saved.” The refrain again in vv. 8, 20.
“Heal me, Yahweh, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved.”
“He who walks whole (תָמִים) shall be saved, but he who is crooked in his ways shall fall at once.”

evidence.locator: Jdg.3.9, וַיּוֹשִׁיעֵם → ἔσωσεν; Psa.118.25, הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא → σῶσον δή; Isa.45.22 וְהִוָּשְׁעוּ → σωθήσεσθε; σῴζω renders יָשַׁע about 120 times. Num.10.9 וְנוֹשַׁעְתֶּם → διασωθήσεσθε; Exo.14.30 וַיּוֹשַׁע → ἐρρύσατο.

evidence.note: “You shall call his name Ἰησοῦς, for he shall save (σώσει) his people from their sins”: the verb explains the name.
“There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy” (the Peshitta adds “and judge”): as Isa 33:22, “Yahweh our judge, Yahweh our lawgiver … he will save us”.

evidence.locator: Jdg.3.9, מוֹשִׁיעַ → σωτῆρα; Isa.43.11 מוֹשִׁיעַ → σῴζων

evidence.note: “Of this man's seed God, according to his promise, raised up (ἤγειρε) for Israel a σωτήρ, Jesus”: the words of Jdg 3:9, 15, where Yahweh raised up a מוֹשִׁיעַ.
“Him God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a σωτήρ, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.”
“To you is born this day in the city of David a σωτήρ, who is Christ the Lord.”
“The living God, who is the σωτήρ of all men, especially of those who believe.”
“To the only wise God our σωτήρ.”
From Hebrew הוֹשַׁע and נָא: the cry of Psa 118:25, הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא, “save now!”

The crowds before and behind him cry “ὡσαννά to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! ὡσαννά in the highest!”: Psa 118:25–26 cried to the king entering Jerusalem. The Peshitta writes it ܐܘܫܥܢܐ.
The children in the temple cry “ὡσαννά to the Son of David”, and the chief priests are angry.
“ὡσαννά! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!”
With palm branches: “ὡσαννά! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”

parallels.note: “Redeem”: the savior is also the redeemer.
“Judge”: to judge for the weak is to save them.

opposites.note: “Distress”, literally a strait place: the time from which one is saved.

evidence.note: “Let them save you in the time of your distress.”

phrases.gloss: and there is none to save
save out of the hand of
my own hand has saved me

words.summary: The commonest noun of the root, above all in the Psalms and Isaiah: the deliverance Yahweh works, and Yahweh himself as the one who brings it.

senses.definition: A deliverance that is seen to happen, chiefly from enemies in war, done by Yahweh (or by a man through him).

evidence.note: At the sea: “Stand still and see יְשׁוּעַת יַהְוֶה, which he will do for you today; the Egyptians you see today you shall never see again.”
“You will not need to fight in this; stand still and see יְשׁוּעַת יַהְוֶה with you.”
The people: shall Jonathan die, “who has worked this great יְשׁוּעָה in Israel? … for he has worked with God this day.”
“To Yahweh belongs הַיְשׁוּעָה; your blessing is on your people.”
From the fish: “יְשׁוּעָתָה לַיַהְוֶה, salvation belongs to Yahweh.”
Many say of me, “There is no יְשׁוּעָה for him in God.”
Joab to Abishai: if Aram is too strong for me, “you shall be to me לִישׁוּעָה”, my help.
After “he will swallow up death for ever” (v. 8): “This is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us … we will be glad and rejoice בִּישׁוּעָתוֹ.” Salvation from death itself.

senses.definition: Yahweh named as the salvation of the one who trusts him: the one in whom deliverance is found.

evidence.note: “Yah is my strength and song, and he has become my יְשׁוּעָה; this is my God.” Repeated in Isa 12:2 and Psa 118:14.
“Behold, God is my יְשׁוּעָה; I will trust and not be afraid.”
Jeshurun forsook God who made him “and despised the rock of his יְשׁוּעָה”.
The king of David's line shall call to Yahweh, “You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my יְשׁוּעָה.”
“I will thank you, for you answered me and have become my יְשׁוּעָה.”

senses.gloss: the salvation awaited, for Israel and the nations
senses.definition: In Genesis, Isaiah and the Psalms, the salvation Yahweh has promised and is waited for, set beside his righteousness, which will be seen to the ends of the earth.

evidence.note: In the midst of Jacob's blessings: “לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִוִּיתִי יַהְוֶה, I wait for your salvation, Yahweh.”
To the servant: “I will give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my יְשׁוּעָה to the end of the earth.” Quoted by Paul and Barnabas in Act 13:47.
“In a time of favour I answered you, and in a day of יְשׁוּעָה I helped you.” Quoted in 2Co 6:2: “now is the day of salvation.”
“All the ends of the earth shall see יְשׁוּעַת אֱלֹהֵינוּ.” Also Psa 98:3.
“Keep justice and do righteousness, for my יְשׁוּעָה is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.”
The heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth wear out like a garment, “but my יְשׁוּעָה will be for ever, and my righteousness will not be broken.”
“Yahweh has made known his יְשׁוּעָה; in the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.”
Yahweh puts on righteousness as a breastplate “and a helmet of יְשׁוּעָה on his head”: taken up in Eph 6:17 and 1Th 5:8.
“With joy you shall draw water from the wells of הַיְשׁוּעָה.”
“You shall call your walls יְשׁוּעָה and your gates Praise.” Also Isa 26:1.
“I will lift up the cup of יְשׁוּעוֹת and call on the name of Yahweh.”

senses.definition: A person's safety or well-being, which can be lost.

evidence.note: “Terrors are turned on me; they pursue my honour like the wind, וּכְעָב עָבְרָה יְשֻׁעָתִי, and my welfare has passed away like a cloud.”
“This also shall be my יְשׁוּעָה, that a godless man shall not come before him.” Paul takes these words for himself in prison: “this will turn out for my σωτηρία” (Php 1:19).

evidence.locator: Exo.14.13, יְשׁוּעַת → σωτηρίαν; Isa.49.6, Isa.49.8, Isa.52.10, Job.13.16 the same; σωτηρία renders יְשׁוּעָה ×36

evidence.note: “So the Lord has commanded us: I have set you as a light of the nations, that you should be for σωτηρίαν to the end of the earth” (Isa 49:6).
Isa 49:8 quoted: “in a day of σωτηρίας I helped you; behold, now is the day of σωτηρίας.”
“This will turn out for my σωτηρίαν”: the words of Job 13:16.
“For a helmet, the hope of σωτηρίας” (Isa 59:17).
“ἡ σωτηρία to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb”, as Psa 3:9 and Jon 2:10.

evidence.locator: Isa.59.17, יְשׁוּעָה → σωτηρίου; Psa.116.13 the same; σωτήριον renders יְשׁוּעָה ×9

evidence.note: “Take the helmet τοῦ σωτηρίου”: Isa 59:17.
Simeon, holding the child: “my eyes have seen your σωτήριον, which you prepared before all peoples, a light for revelation to the nations” (Luk 2:30–32), in the words of Isa 52:10 and 49:6.

parallels.note: Yahweh's “righteousness”, set beside his salvation in Isaiah and the Psalms.

words.summary: A shorter noun with much the sense of יְשׁוּעָה, nearly all in the Psalms and the prophets, most often with a suffix: “my salvation”, “the God of my salvation”. In Job it is the safety of a man set out of reach of harm.

senses.definition: The deliverance God gives, and God named as its source: “the God of my salvation”, “the horn of my salvation”.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is my crag, my stronghold and my deliverer (מְפַלְטִי) … my shield and קֶרֶן יִשְׁעִי, the horn of my salvation, my high tower.” Also 2Sa 22:3. Zechariah takes up the phrase: God “has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David” (Luk 1:69).
“Yahweh is my light וְיִשְׁעִי, and my salvation; whom shall I fear?”
Though the fig does not blossom and the flock is cut off, “I will rejoice in Yahweh, I will exult in the God of my salvation.” Mary's words in Luk 1:47 are those of this verse in Greek.
“I will look to Yahweh, I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.”
“You are the God of my salvation; for you I wait all the day.”
“You have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the rock of your stronghold.”
“Surely his salvation is near those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.”
“You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed.”
David's last words: an everlasting covenant, “for all my salvation and all my desire, will he not make it grow?”

senses.gloss: salvation that comes; garments of salvation
senses.definition: In Isaiah, salvation as something that comes to Zion, springs from the earth with righteousness, and clothes those whom Yahweh saves.

evidence.note: “Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, יִשְׁעֵךְ בָּא, your salvation comes; behold, his reward is with him”: salvation spoken of as a person who comes. Matthew opens his quotation of Zec 9:9 with this verse's “Say to the daughter of Zion” (Mat 21:5).
“Let the earth open, and let them bear fruit, יֶשַׁע, and let righteousness spring up together.”
“He has clothed me with בִּגְדֵי יֶשַׁע, garments of salvation; he has covered me with the robe of righteousness.”
“Her priests I will clothe with salvation.”
“My righteousness is near, my salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples.”

senses.definition: Being out of harm's reach: the condition of one who has been saved.

evidence.note: The fool's children “are far from safety (מִיֶּשַׁע), crushed in the gate, with none to deliver”.
God sets the lowly on high, “and those who mourn are lifted to safety”.
“Because of the plundering of the poor … I will now arise, says Yahweh; I will set him in the safety he longs for.”

evidence.locator: Psa.18.3, קֶרֶן יִשְׁעִי → κέρας σωτηρίας; σωτηρία renders יֵשַׁע ×12

evidence.note: “He has raised up a horn of salvation (κέρας σωτηρίας) for us in the house of David his servant”: the phrase of Psa 18:3.

evidence.locator: Hab.3.18, בֵּאלֹהֵי יִשְׁעִי → ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτῆρί μου; Mic.7.7 and Isa.62.11 likewise σωτήρ

evidence.note: “My spirit has rejoiced in God my savior (ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτῆρί μου)”: Hab 3:18.

words.summary: Deliverance, very often the victory Yahweh gives in a battle, and with it the lesson that this victory comes from Yahweh and not from horses, armies or men.

senses.definition: The victory won in a battle, said to be worked or given by Yahweh, even when a man fights it.

evidence.note: After the rescue of Jabesh-gilead: “No man shall be put to death this day, for today Yahweh has worked תְּשׁוּעָה in Israel.”
Eleazar struck the Philistines until his hand clung to the sword, “and Yahweh worked a great תְּשׁוּעָה that day”. Also v. 12.
Naaman, “for by him Yahweh had given תְּשׁוּעָה to Aram”: victory, given by Yahweh even to a foreign army.
David struck the Philistine, “and Yahweh worked a great תְּשׁוּעָה for all Israel”.
Samson: “You have given this great תְּשׁוּעָה by the hand of your servant.”
Elisha at the window: “the arrow of Yahweh's תְּשׁוּעָה, the arrow of תְּשׁוּעָה against Aram.”

senses.definition: Deliverance considered as to its source: not horse, army or man, but Yahweh.

evidence.note: “The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but הַתְּשׁוּעָה is Yahweh's.”
“A horse is a false hope for תְשׁוּעָה, and by its great strength it shall not deliver.”
“Do not trust in nobles, in a son of man, in whom there is no תְשׁוּעָה.”
“Give us help against the adversary, for vain is the תְּשׁוּעָה of man.” Also Psa 108:13.
“Truly in vain is the noise on the hills; truly in Yahweh our God is the תְּשׁוּעָה of Israel.”
“The תְּשׁוּעָה of the righteous is from Yahweh, their stronghold in the time of distress.”

senses.definition: In Proverbs, the safe outcome that many counsellors bring, in war or in a people's affairs.

evidence.note: “Where there is no guidance a people falls, but in many counsellors there is תְשׁוּעָה.”
“By wise guidance you make war, and in many counsellors there is תְשׁוּעָה.”

senses.definition: The salvation the faithful wait for and long for, which Yahweh brings near and makes everlasting.

evidence.note: “Israel is saved by Yahweh with תְּשׁוּעַת עוֹלָמִים, an everlasting salvation.”
“I bring near my righteousness … and my תְּשׁוּעָה will not delay; I will give תְּשׁוּעָה in Zion.”
“It is good that one should wait quietly for the תְּשׁוּעָה of Yahweh.”
“My soul longs for your תְּשׁוּעָה; I hope in your word.”
“Deliver me from bloodguilt, God, God of my תְּשׁוּעָה.”

evidence.locator: 1Sa.11.13, Isa.45.17, Psa.37.39, תְּשׁוּעָה → σωτηρία; σωτηρία renders תְּשׁוּעָה ×27, βοήθεια ×2 (Pro.21.31)

opposites.note: The horse is a “lie”, a false hope, for victory.

words.summary: Found once, in the plural: God's acts of deliverance, set beside escapes from death.

senses.definition: Deliverances, in the plural, which God works for his people, parallel to “ways out from death”.

evidence.note: “God is to us a God לְמוֹשָׁעוֹת, of deliverances, and to Yahweh the Lord belong the ways out (תּוֹצָאוֹת) from death.”

words.summary: Twice, in a pair with a word for a nobleman: a man of standing and means. Its tie to ישע “save” is not clear from scripture; Arabic wasiʿa, which has both “be wide” and “be rich, ample in means”, may bridge the two, but that is a possibility only. Two other tokens listed under its BDB key (Isa 22:5 “outcry” and Ezk 23:23, the people Shoa) are other words.

senses.definition: A man of rank or wealth, set beside a prince or a noble and over against the poor.

evidence.note: God “does not show partiality to princes (שָׂרִים), nor regard שׁוֹעַ more than the poor (דָל), for they are all the work of his hands”.
“The fool shall no more be called noble (נָדִיב), nor the scoundrel said to be שׁוֹעַ.”

evidence.locator: Job.34.19, שׁוֹעַ → τιμή; Isa.32.5 has σίγα (the translator read another word)

words.summary: Once, in Job 36:19, where the sense is uncertain: “riches” beside “all the forces of strength”, or a “cry” (as שֶׁוַע from שׁוע “cry for help”). Its tie to ישע rests only on the adjective שׁוֹעַ and the Arabic sense “ample in means”; the link to the root is not clear. Most tokens under its BDB key are the name Shua (Gen 38:2 and others), which is not this word.

senses.definition: In Elihu's words, something a man might set out before God to buy his way out of distress, which God will not value.

evidence.note: “Will he value שׁוּעֲךָ, that you be not in distress (בְצָר), or all the forces of strength?”: following v. 18, “let not a great ransom turn you aside”, wealth is the likelier sense.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܐܘܫܥܢܐ (ʾōšaʿnā), the cry of the crowds at Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, where the Greek has ὡσαννά. It is the Hebrew prayer הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא of Psa 118:25 kept as a word: the only word of this root in the Peshitta, whose verb for “save” is another root (ܦܪܩ, ܚܝܐ).

senses.definition: A cry of praise and petition to the king who comes in the name of Yahweh, taken from Psa 118:25–26.

evidence.note: “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
The children cry it in the temple.
“Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”

cognates.gloss: be wide, roomy, ample; II wassaʿa make wide, make room, enlarge (contrary of ḍayyaqa, straiten); saʿa width, ampleness of life, wealth
cognates.note: Arabic initial w answers to Hebrew initial y (as wlad / ילד), s to Hebrew ש, and ʿ to ע. The Arabic is wide, roomy, and so unstraitened, provided for, rich. It fits the Hebrew's setting: one is saved out of צָרָה, distress, a strait place (Jdg 10:14), and scripture's own picture of deliverance is being brought out into a wide place: “in distress you made room for me” (בַּצָּר הִרְחַבְתָּ לִּי, Psa 4:2), “he brought me out into a broad place” (Psa 18:20). The Arabic sense “wealth, ample means” also fits the adjective שׁוֹעַ, “man of means”.

evidence.note: “The vessel was sufficient in its capacity … or large, for the goods”; “He (God) made his means of subsistence ample and abundant.”

“He made wide, broad, spacious, roomy, or ample … He made room, or ample space, for him”; “(God) amplified … his means of subsistence; contr. of ضَيَّقَ”; form IV “made the thing ample, or free from straitness, to him … O God, make thy mercy sufficient for us … He (God) enriched him”; VIII “It (a man's state) became free from straitness”.
“Width; breadth … Ampleness of the means, or circumstances, of life … richness, or wealthiness, or competence”.

cognates.gloss: (Sabaean, causative) bestow, grant; give aid (said of a god); st- stem ask the assistance of
cognates.note: Sabaic. The causative is said of a god who aids his worshipper, “aided and protected his servant when they campaigned”: the help of a god in war, as with the Hebrew hiphil. Sabaic keeps s¹ (Hebrew ש) and ʿ apart from the sounds they merged with in Hebrew.

evidence.locator: p. 152, root WS¹ʿ, h pf hws¹ʿ
evidence.note: “BESTOW, GRANT; GIVE AID (2nd obj with b-; said of a god) [Ar wsʿ D ‘be generous’ …] … J629/25: hws¹ʿ whwfyn ʿbdhw … bkn sbʾw ‘(the god) aided and protected His servant when they campaigned’”; st pf stws¹ʿ “ASK THE ASSISTANCE OF”.

cognates.gloss: (Moabite) he saved me; [high place of] salvation
cognates.note: Mesha king of Moab (2Ki 3:4) says he made a high place for Kemosh “because he saved me (השעני) from all the assailants and let me look on all my foes”: the causative of this root, in the same sense of deliverance from enemies, spelled without the y as Moabite writes such forms. The high place is probably named “[high place of] salvation”, ישע, though the word is partly restored. The king's own name, משע, is the Hebrew מֵישַׁע.

evidence.note: Line 3 ואעש הבמת זאת לכמש בקרחה ב[נס י]; line 4 שע כי השעני מכל השלכן וכי הראני בכל שנאי.
“And I made this high place for Kemôš in Ḳrḥh. [High place of sal]vation, for he had saved me from all the assailants (?), and because he had caused me to look upon all my foes.”

doctrine.statement: Israel going to war was to blow the trumpets, be remembered before Yahweh, and so “be saved from your enemies” (Num 10:9). The victory is never put down to the army: “Yahweh does not save with sword and spear, for the battle is Yahweh's” (1Sa 17:47); “the horse is made ready for the day of battle, but salvation is Yahweh's” (Pro 21:31; Psa 33:16–17); Gideon's army was cut down lest Israel say “my own hand has saved me” (Jdg 7:2), and Israel did not win the land by its own arm (Psa 44:4). Even a heathen general's victory was Yahweh's gift (2Ki 5:1). To take saving into one's own hands is what Abigail kept David from (1Sa 25:26, 33), and the wise man is told “do not say, I will repay evil; wait for Yahweh, and he will save you” (Pro 20:22). From the verses: deliverance in every form is Yahweh's to give, and the part of those he saves is to call on him and wait for him (Psa 18:4; Lam 3:26).

Yahweh says “beside me there is no savior” (Isa 43:11; 45:21; Hos 13:4); yet when Israel cried out, “Yahweh raised up a savior” (Jdg 3:9, 15), “gave Israel a savior” (2Ki 13:5), “gave them saviors” (Neh 9:27). The two are not in tension: the men are saviors because Yahweh raises and sends them, and the salvation they bring is his. Moses renamed Hoshea, “salvation”, as Joshua, “Yahweh saves” (Num 13:16), the man who led Israel into the land. The angel names Mary's son Ἰησοῦς, the same name, “for he shall save his people from their sins” (Mat 1:21), and Paul says “of this man's seed God according to his promise raised up for Israel a Savior, Jesus” (Act 13:23), in the very words of Judges; Peter, “him God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Savior” (Act 5:31). From the verses: Jesus is the savior whom Yahweh, the only Savior, raised up and gave, as he raised up the judges, and God is called “the Savior of all men” because the salvation is his (1Ti 4:10; Jud 1:25).

The verb begins with rescue from enemies, but scripture carries it further. Yahweh promises to “save them out of all their dwellings in which they sinned, and cleanse them” (Ezk 37:23; 36:29); Jerusalem is told “wash your heart from wickedness, that you may be saved” (Jer 4:14), and the nations “turn to me and be saved” (Isa 45:22). David asks “deliver me from bloodguilt, God of my salvation” (Psa 51:16). Isaiah sets the salvation they waited for beside the swallowing up of death for ever (Isa 25:8–9), which Paul says is fulfilled when the dead are raised incorruptible (1Co 15:52–54); and to Yahweh belong “the ways out from death” (Psa 68:21). Jesus is named “for he shall save his people from their sins” (Mat 1:21). From the verses: the salvation scripture promises is from sin, by repentance and cleansing, and from death, by resurrection; its last enemy is death.

Jacob waited for Yahweh's salvation (Gen 49:18). Isaiah says Yahweh's servant would be “my salvation to the end of the earth” (Isa 49:6), that “all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God” (Isa 52:10), and calls them “turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth” (Isa 45:22). Simeon, holding the child Jesus, said “my eyes have seen your salvation … a light for revelation to the nations” (Luk 2:30–32); Paul and Barnabas, turning to the nations at Antioch, said the Lord had commanded them in Isa 49:6 (Act 13:46–47), and Paul quotes Isa 49:8, “now is the day of salvation” (2Co 6:2). From the verses: the salvation promised to Israel was always meant to reach the nations, through the servant, and the apostles preached it so.

note: Left out: יָשְׁפֶה “jasper” (j.dy.ar, Exo 28:20; 39:13; Ezk 28:13), a loan filed under ישׁע by spelling only: Akkadian (y)ašpû, Greek ἴασπις, Persian yašm point to a non-Semitic stone name, not this root; it needs its own entry (root ישפה). Proper names are left for name entries, none written here: Isaiah/Jeshaiah יְשַׁעְיָהוּ, יְשַׁעְיָה (j.dy.ai, j.dy.aj), Hoshea הוֹשֵׁעַ (j.dy.ak), Ishi יִשְׁעִי (j.dy.ah, whose key also holds many tokens of “my salvation”, יֵשַׁע + suffix), Hoshaiah (j.dy.al), Mesha מֵישַׁע/מֵישָׁע (j.dy.ao, j.dy.ap), Shua שׁוּעַ, שׁוּעָא (j.dy.ae, j.dy.ag), and Joshua/Jeshua יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, which BDB files under הוה (j.dy.am); Abishua, Elishua, Malchishua and Bathshua likewise. BDB's cross-reference keys (e.bc.ae, e.bc.af הוֹשַׁעְנָה, m.bd.ae, m.bw.ai, v.bv.ae, w.bq.bj) have no tokens and are not claimed. The keys j.dy.ad and j.dy.af also count tokens that are other words (Isa 22:5 שׁוֹעַ “outcry”, Ezk 23:23 Shoa; the name Shua). שׁוֹעַ and שׁוּעַ are kept with their link to the root unclear; Job 36:19 might instead be שֶׁוַע “cry” of שׁוע. Ugaritic not found in Segert's glossary; Ge'ez ʾawšəʿa “answer” (noted by Biella) not followed up in Dillmann/Leslau. The Peshitta's NT renders σῴζω by ܚܝܐ and ܦܪܩ, not this root; ܐܘܫܥܢܐ is SEDRA lexeme 63 (root 52).
